ctor.rationale: `base(1, CardType.Attack, CardRarity.Uncommon, TargetType.AnyEnemy)` (Rampage.cs:40-43) == cost 1 / ATTACK / UNCOMMON / ANY_ENEMY.

CanonicalVars.rationale: `new DamageVar(9m, ValueProp.Move)` + `new DynamicVar("Increase", 5m)` (Rampage.cs:18-22) == both numbers, both declared, and `_increase` is in `Card._MAGIC_ATTRS` so `magic_number` surfaces it.

OnPlay.rationale: `await DamageCmd.Attack(DynamicVars.Damage.BaseValue)...Execute()` then `DynamicVars.Damage.BaseValue += DynamicVars["Increase"].BaseValue` (Rampage.cs:48-52) == `DamageCmd.deal(...)` then `self._damage += self._increase`. The order is load-bearing on both sides -- THIS play uses the pre-increment damage -- and the growth persists on the card instance for the rest of the combat, which the sim's docstring states explicitly.

OnUpgrade.rationale: `DynamicVars["Increase"].UpgradeValueBy(4m)` (Rampage.cs:63) == `self._increase += 4` (5 -> 9). The BASE damage stays 9 when upgraded on both sides -- only the growth rate changes, which is the easy one to get backwards.
